quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 1999 Paper Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 1999 paper, covering calculus, matrices and determinants, vectors and 3D, integrals and probability. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics 1999 previous year paper

questions.q: If y = e^(2x), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx e^(u) = e^(u) du/dx. Here u = 2x, so du/dx = 2 and dy/dx = 2e^(2x).

questions.q: The value of the determinant | 2 3 ; 4 5 | is:

questions.explanation: The integral of 1/x is the natural logarithm: ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C.

questions.q: The angle between two vectors a and b when a · b = 0 (both non-zero) is:
questions.explanation: a · b = |a||b|cosθ. A zero dot product with non-zero vectors forces cosθ = 0, so θ = 90° (the vectors are perpendicular).

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed twice. The probability of getting exactly one head is:
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one head occurs in HT and TH, so the probability is 2/4 = 1/2.

questions.q: The derivative of sin x with respect to x is:
questions.explanation: The standard result is d/dx (sin x) = cos x.

questions.q: If A is a 3x3 matrix with det(A) = 5, then det(2A) equals:
questions.explanation: For an n x n matrix, det(kA) = k^n det(A). Here n = 3, so det(2A) = 2^3 × 5 = 8 × 5 = 40.

questions.q: The direction ratios of the line joining points (1, 2, 3) and (4, 6, 3) are:
questions.explanation: Direction ratios are the differences of coordinates: (4-1, 6-2, 3-3) = (3, 4, 0).

faq.q: Is the CBSE Class 12 Maths 1999 paper still useful for today's board exam?
faq.a: Yes. The 1999 paper predates the current pattern, but its core topics — calculus, matrices and determinants, vectors, 3D geometry and probability — are still the backbone of the Class 12 syllabus. Older papers are excellent for building fundamentals, even if the exact format has changed.

faq.q: How is the 1999 paper different from recent CBSE papers?
faq.a: The 1999 paper has no MCQ or case-study section and follows the older marking scheme with mostly long-answer questions. Recent papers mix objective, short-answer and case-based questions. Use 1999 for concept practice and a recent sample paper for exam-format practice.

faq.q: Which chapters carry the most weight in this paper?
faq.a: Calculus — differentiation, integration and their applications — dominates, as it still does today. Matrices and determinants, vectors and 3D geometry, and probability together make up most of the rest.

faq.q: Should I time myself while solving this paper?
faq.a: Once you have revised the chapters, yes. Sitting the paper in a single timed session shows you where you slow down — usually long integration or 3D problems — so you can plan your exam time better.
